title: Grateful Dead Live at Sound City Recording Studios on 1966-01-29

ai_review.summary: Historical Acid Test recording with thin soundboard mix; interesting for fans but not a true Grateful Dead concert.
ai_review.review: The file captures the January 29, 1966 Merry Pranksters acid‑test session rather than a musical performance, offering brief snippets of the band amid spoken interviews. The soundboard source is present but the mix is thin – background instruments are often missing and Jerry Garcia’s vocals sound “shot,” leading many listeners to view it as more of a curiosity than a showcase of the Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: While several reviewers give high star ratings for historical interest, most comment that the recording lacks musical substance and suffers from poor mix quality, pulling the overall assessment toward average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Soundboard capture but very thin mix – background instruments largely absent, vocal clarity poor (Jerry’s voice described as “shot”), occasional tape hiss; some note it is clearer than earlier test recordings.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Not a conventional set; the recording consists of interview excerpts, spoken Prankster dialogue, and brief musical fragments from the Acid Test session.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice is reported as barely audible and “shot” on track 10, though he does appear briefly.
